dedupe_keys.name: australia s mobile black spot program and its anao audits and evaluation

description: This investment appraisal and policy evaluation case concerns Australia's Mobile Black Spot Program, which since 2015 has co-funded new or upgraded mobile base stations in regional and remote areas with poor coverage, partly to improve access to emergency calls. The Australian National Audit Office's Report No. 10 of 2016-17 examined the first round, in which Telstra and Vodafone were funded to build 499 base stations with about A$385 million of Commonwealth, state and operator money; it found that the department had set up the elements of a competitive merit-based grants programme, but that about 39 sites would have been built anyway and some 89 sites, which received about A$28 million, gave minimal new coverage, so much of the round consolidated existing coverage, and it recommended better assessment criteria, methodology and performance measurement. Later audits reviewed further rounds and election commitments, and the department commissioned a programme evaluation. Coverage: Australia, rounds from 2015 onwards. Format and access: free audit reports on the ANAO website and a free evaluation report from the department. Caveats: audits judge administration and value for money, not network resilience directly; coverage benefits are modelled. Simulation uses: capacity planning of rural mobile coverage, cost and benefit inputs for coverage investment, and emergency-call access in bushfire and flood prone areas. Related records: the Optus 2023 outage review covers Triple Zero access, and national coverage maps from regulators give the baseline.
